Before choosing a cloud platform, finish this sentence: “This move should make it easier for our team to…”

That answer gives a migration a business purpose. Maybe people need better access to shared documents. Maybe an aging application needs a new home. The right plan depends on the work you need to support.

We at Cloud2e provide cloud adoption and migration services, including cloud strategy and Microsoft 365 adoption. That means helping organizations move from on-premises systems into cloud services and adopt the tools people will use afterward.

For a useful starting conversation, pick one application. Identify its users, the information it handles, the other systems it needs, and who will support it after the move.

Then define how you will check that everyday work still functions. A successful sign-in alone does not answer that question.

What business problem would you want your next cloud project to solve?

posts.company:
A migration plan needs a definition of “ready for everyday use.”

Moving an application or a collection of files is one milestone. Employees also need to find their information, complete their usual tasks, and know where to get help.

Cloud2e offers cloud adoption and Microsoft 365 services, including on-premises migration and cloud strategy. Our Microsoft 365 service areas include SharePoint, Teams, OneDrive, and Exchange Online.

When preparing a move, select a small set of real business tasks to check before the broader rollout. Ask the people who perform those tasks to help define the checks. Include access to the right documents, collaboration with colleagues, and the support process if something fails.

Document what must work, who confirms it, and what happens if a check does not pass. Those decisions give the project a clearer finish line.
